content:
Orignal error message

error: elaboration function for … has not been implemented

While trying to organize some custom notations so that they'd all be defined under the same Notation namespace (so they could be selectively enabled by opening the Notation namespace) I've run into a surprising error. I have reduced the setup to trigger the error into the following MWE.

The MWE this time requires a couple of files, so I can't provide a link to the Lean playground.

File setup for MWE

File Other.lean
module

@[expose] public section

namespace Mwe

scoped notation (name := Notation.arrow) conf:40 " -ᵖ-> " conf':41 => (· = ·) conf conf'
File Basic.lean:
module

public import Mwe.Other

open Mwe.Notation

@[expose] public section

#check Mwe.Notation.arrow

theorem purePrimStep_of_pureBaseStep {e₁ e₂ : Expr} :
    e₁ = e₂ →
    e₁ -ᵖ-> e₂ := sorry

The error I get in e₁ -ᵖ-> e₂ says

elaboration function for Mwe.Notation.arrow has not been implemented

It seems like the definition at least is found, as shown by the #check command just before, so maybe this is an issue with elaboration order? Funnily enough, if instead of specifying the namespace in the (name := ...) of the notation command I do so outside, things seem to work fine.

Working version of Other.lean

File Other.lean
module

@[expose] public section

namespace Mwe.Notation

scoped notation (name := arrow) conf:40 " -ᵖ-> " conf':41 => (· = ·) conf conf'

If you do open Mwe (or open scoped Mwe, if you want to be more restrictive) in Basic.lean, does the notation start working?

I'm guessing that using name like this isn't supported, or at least not currently supported. I'm expecting scoped to add it to the current namespace, not the namespace the definition is immediately in.

Kyle Miller said:

If you do open Mwe (or open scoped Mwe, if you want to be more restrictive) in Basic.lean, does the notation start working?

I'm guessing that using name like this isn't supported, or at least not currently supported. I'm expecting scoped to add it to the current namespace, not the namespace the definition is immediately in.

That seemed to work. I find surprising that this notation is not supported, because I've used it elsewhere and it seemes to behave as I expected. I should probably change that code then!

Fernando LEAL said:

because I've used it elsewhere and it seemes to behave as I expected

By this I mean that, at least in a single file, it seems to behave as expected.
Althought it is true that the scoped modifier forces the notation to happen inside of another namespace than the one given in the (name := iden) identifier.

For Lean to support (name := ns.ident) in syntax, it would need to do a similar trick to how def ns.ident works, which is it rewrites itself to wrap def ident in a variant of the namespace ns command, one that keeps scoped items active.
Isn't all notation (name := iden) transformed into syntax (name := iden), which is then transformed to meta def iden : Lean.ParserDescr?

Hmm, good point that it's a macro. I missed the subtlety that the syntax is scoped to the right namespace, but the elaborator isn't.

What behavior do you see with open scoped Mwe, vs open scoped Mwe.Notation, vs open scoped Mwe Mwe.Notation? Could you let me know two things for each: (1) does the syntax parse? and (2) if so, does it elaborate? This would be helpful to pinpoint the issue.

Command executed prior to use Syntax? Elaboration?
None :cross_mark: :cross_mark:
open scoped Mwe :cross_mark: :grey_question:
open scoped Mwe.Notation :check: :cross_mark:
open scoped Mwe.Notation Mwe :check: :check:
